findings.claim: Default execution path is the orchestrator's built-in offline paper broker only. Orchestrator.__init__ hard-constructs CostedPaperBrokerAdapter and has no broker parameter. _assert_paper_plant_broker only enforces the broker type in PAPER_APPLY, and the startup certificate is self-asserted with passed=True; StartupGate.certify_startup is not called by the orchestrator. The sealed candidate script uses PAPER_APPLY, closed_loop_mode=active_paper, governor_authority from the protocol (default 'advisory'), and an in-memory CentralPlantMasterDCS. It passes neither combined_cycle_runtime nor paper_journal. Within this snapshot there is no call site for CombinedCycleRuntime(, PaperStateJournal(, .restore( or .restore_snapshot(, and there are no test files. So CC runtime, journal, restore and Engine B are opt-in code that the sealed candidate path never exercises.
findings.impact: A passing import or helper test of the CC, journal or Engine B modules says nothing about the sealed calibration path. Conversely, defects in those modules do not affect the sealed candidate numbers.
findings.action: Label evidence per mode (SHADOW, PAPER_APPLY advisory, PAPER_APPLY full, +CC, +journal). Add a harness case per mode that goes through Revision2ExternalEngineOrchestrator.run.

findings.claim: By static reading, the paper broker never sets 'product' on a position at fill time, but CombinedCycleRuntime.reconcile compares position.get('product') (no default) to record.product ('MIS' for A_OPEN). PaperBrokerAdapter._apply_fill_to_position creates {quantity, avg_price} only, and get_position returns that dict. Only request_product_conversion writes position['product']. Other paths default with .get('product','MIS'): ensure_protection, snapshot and the conversion receipt. reconcile() is called unconditionally in handle_bar for every open CC position. The first bar after any A_OPEN fill would therefore raise CombinedCycleReconciliationError('broker quantity/product differs'). This was not executed, and the snapshot has no tests that would have caught it.
findings.impact: If confirmed, enabling combined_cycle_runtime aborts the run on the first bar after the first fill.
findings.action: Add a one-fill, one-bar test with CC runtime and a real CostedPaperBrokerAdapter. Fix by defaulting to 'MIS' in reconcile, or by writing the product at fill time.

findings.claim: The paper broker never resets position['product'] when a position goes flat. After a MIS->CNC conversion and close, the symbol's position dict stays {quantity:0, product:'CNC'}. A later fill on the same symbol reuses that dict. register_fill then calls ensure_protection(product=record.product='MIS'), which raises ValueError('Paper protection does not match position'). This runs after the broker fill and after open_trades is populated (see F04).
findings.impact: A B-handoff followed by re-entry in the same symbol in the same run leaves a filled broker position with an incomplete engine ledger.
findings.action: Reset product on flat and test conversion -> close -> re-entry.

findings.claim: Entry post-fill sequencing is not atomic. The broker fill happens at 2008. Then come post-fill checks, observe_fill and entry_snapshot (2036-2086), then open_trades is assigned (2087), then _register_position_lifecycle, which may call CC store.save and ensure_protection (2102). Only after that do governor.begin_position, entry_bar_index and exit_controller.open_position run (2103-2109). A raise at 2051-2052, in observe_fill, in entry_snapshot, or in register_fill propagates with the broker already holding the position. Depending on where it raised, either open_trades lacks the trade (unowned broker position) or open_trades has it but entry_bar_index, exit state and governor state are missing. There is no compensating close or halt. The CC store and the paper journal are separate SQLite files with no shared transaction.
findings.impact: A post-fill persistence failure leaves broker and ledger inconsistent. Under the journal this is only detected at the next checkpoint (paper_state_journal.py:155-159), and the exception has already aborted the tick.
findings.action: Reorder so all in-memory ownership state is set before durable writes. Wrap post-fill bookkeeping in a handler that flags and halts or flattens. Define one atomic commit boundary across the journal and CC store.

findings.claim: The two restart mechanisms are mutually exclusive, and the CC restore path is incomplete. PaperStateJournal.bind requires a fresh engine (no fills, open_trades or completed_trades) and recovers by replaying from the start. CombinedCycleRuntime.restore writes engine.open_trades from the store, so bind would reject it. A replay against an existing store would collide in register_fill (expected_revision=0). Separately, restore() rebuilds only open_trades, _position_lifecycle, Engine B state and the _trade_sequence floor. Not restored: entry_bar_index (local variable in run()), _exit_controller_states, governor.begin_position, the daily baseline and symbol lockouts, the closed-loop ledger, and the conviction/HMM histories. After restore, held=bar_idx-entry_bar_index.get(symbol,bar_idx)=0 on every bar for an A_OPEN position, so maximum_hold_bars and minimum_hold never trigger. With state None, close feedback is skipped (the 'if state is not None' guard) and bars_held is None. On the first tick _active_trading_date is None, so _day_start_equity is re-based and symbol_tripped, cooldowns and consecutive_losses are cleared mid-session.
findings.impact: No supported restart exists for CC positions. A hand-assembled restart loses hold-limit enforcement, lockouts, daily loss baseline and close feedback.
findings.action: Decide one recovery model. Either extend the journal to cover CC state, or persist exit-controller, entry_bar_index, lockout and daily-baseline state in the CC snapshot. Add a kill-and-restart test mid-position.

findings.claim: Journal checkpoint temporal consistency is good for what it covers but partial. Checkpoints are committed at the end of each unique-timestamp tick, after all symbols. They are hash-chained, and the prefix is compared on replay. Broker positions are reconciled against open_trades before commit. Covered: plant state, open_trades, broker positions and fills, completed_trades, pnl and costs, close receipts, symbol cooldowns and trips, execution_halted. Not in the payload: _exit_controller_states, entry_bar_index, ECS _previous_demand, portfolio weights, ticks_since_reweight, the closed-loop ledger, conviction/HMM histories, _intent_ledger and _mtm_peak. Divergence there is detected only if it later changes hashed state. The final checkpoint is labelled 'FINAL' and follows end-of-run exits. bind() runs `git ls-files`, so it needs a git checkout; this snapshot has no .git.
findings.impact: Replay verification is strong for ledger and broker state, and silent on controller-internal state. It is also not a live-broker recovery, as the module header says.
findings.action: State the verification scope explicitly. Optionally add a digest of the controller states to the checkpoint.

findings.claim: Close-feedback exactly-once is in-process only (the docstring says so). The order is: ledger close (972-991), then realized-R feedback (1003-1021), then research telemetry. _register_realized_r_close_feedback sets PENDING, then calls merit_source.register_trade, then in PAPER_APPLY bay.register_outcome (else governor.register_trade), then sets DONE. If the second call raises, the first is already applied, the receipt stays PENDING, retries are blocked, and the exception propagates. The close is never re-fed and the two feedback sinks diverge. Receipts are not in the CC store. The journal checkpoint covers _close_feedback_receipts only for deterministic replay. Feedback is also skipped when bay_id is unmapped or when state is None. In PAPER_APPLY, native bay.register_outcome also maintains its own consecutive_stops and tripped_offline, separate from the orchestrator's symbol_tripped.
findings.impact: A crash or exception between ledger close and feedback permanently loses that outcome from dispatch and governor state outside journal replay. Partial feed is possible.
findings.action: Persist receipts and the realized-R in the same transaction as the close. Make the feedback replayable and idempotent per sink.

findings.claim: _execute_exit has no else-branch for result['passed'] being False. A rejected paper exit order is silently ignored: no raise, no halt, no event, though _exit_orders_submitted was already incremented. The position stays in open_trades. At end of run the same call leaves the position open without a report flag. Also, within the 'passed' branch, step 1 calls _close_position_lifecycle (which may call the CC store) before 'del self.open_trades[symbol]'. A raise there leaves completed_trades appended, the broker flat, and open_trades still set.
findings.impact: A failed close is invisible. The 'ledger consistent with broker' comment at 967-971 does not hold if the CC store write fails.
findings.action: Raise or halt on a failed exit. Move del open_trades before the fallible lifecycle write, or make both transactional.

findings.claim: Live broker incompatibility is structural. The orchestrator calls broker.place_order(symbol, side, quantity, order_type, market_price, config, parameter_registry) and reads result['filled_price'], ['filled_quantity'] and ['ack_elapsed_seconds'] (also get_position, fills, realized_pnl and booked_costs). KiteConnectBrokerAdapter.place_order has a different signature (limit_price, exchange, product, correlation_id) and no market_price or config. It returns {accepted, filled:False, status:'ACCEPTED'} with no price or quantity, so the call would raise TypeError. The Kite adapter has no get_position, fills, ensure_protection, request_product_conversion or conversion_receipt. The CC runtime requires the last three; CostedPaperBrokerAdapter is the only class that has them. The orchestrator also passes no product, so a CNC exit would default to MIS on Kite. Kite convert_position returns {passed, product_confirmed} with no UNKNOWN/PENDING/TIMEOUT status or persisted receipt, while the CC runtime expects those statuses. Kite's own safeguards are sound in isolation: no blind retry, tag-based correlation, and position-diff confirmation of conversion.
findings.impact: The engine cannot be driven by the Kite adapter without a new execution layer. Asynchronous acknowledgement, partial fills, rejects and product handling are all unmodelled in the engine.
findings.action: Define a broker port interface that both adapters implement, with async fill and receipt semantics. Do not wire live until the port and reconciliation are tested against a fake that returns delayed, partial and unknown outcomes.

findings.claim: BrokerReconciliationService has no call site in this snapshot. The CC runtime does its own paper-only reconcile (exact-equality stop check, ensure_protection order lookup). The service has richer logic: holdings, duplicate keys, unknown pending orders, SL/SL-M geometry, and trigger tolerance that accepts a tighter broker stop. Nothing connects it to restore() or to the conversion path.
findings.impact: The 'reconciliation' that exists in the runtime path is the paper-only one. Live-style reconciliation is dead code until wired.
findings.action: Wire the service into restore() and into handle_bar's conversion path, and test it against a fake Kite snapshot.

findings.claim: Conversion unknown or late acknowledgement is fail-closed but has no recovery path. _receipt raises CombinedCycleReconciliationError for a missing, UNKNOWN or PENDING receipt. HandoffManager.resolve raises ValueError for an acknowledgement after the deadline or on a different date. Either aborts the whole run with the position still persisted as TRANSFER_REQUESTED (Engine A, MIS) while the broker may already be CNC. Nothing flattens the position or advances the lifecycle; the next restore() reconcile would fail on product mismatch. TIMEOUT is accepted by resolve but nothing produces it. request() returns an existing REJECTED request and so never retries. The paper adapter always acknowledges synchronously, so the UNKNOWN and late paths are unexercised by the default broker. The 15:10-15:14 handoff window (HandoffConfig start/deadline) falls before the force-close time, but nothing here reads force_close_time.
findings.impact: A single ambiguous conversion halts all position management and can strand an MIS-labelled position near square-off.
findings.action: Add an explicit RECONCILE_REQUIRED state and an operator or broker-truth resolver that the runtime calls instead of raising. Test UNKNOWN, late-ACK and ack-after-close cases with a fake adapter.

findings.claim: Next-bar trailing stop ordering is correct in the traced paths, and I found no look-ahead. In _maybe_exit, current_stop is captured (1144-1154) before exit_controller.update (1188) and before path actuation (1213-1217). governor_stop_price is written in _governor_position_step (780-787) after the stop test, and the event is tagged effective_from NEXT_BAR. Controller and governor EXITs are armed and executed at the next bar's open, with stop_gap and target_gap taking precedence (1155-1175). Engine B proposes its stop after the protective tests (183-189) and arms it for the next bar, and its pending exit executes on a later bar's open. Qualifier: while a position is B_OPEN, handle_bar returns True, so the governor position step, exit-PID state updates and MFE/MAE observation never run for it. Under governor_authority='full', Engine B is the only discretionary exit authority for B positions; MFE/MAE for B trades are stale.
findings.impact: No ordering defect found. Authority boundary: 'full' governor does not govern B_OPEN positions.
findings.action: Document the authority split. Add a trailing-ordering regression test over A and B paths.

findings.claim: B session and gap policy is minimal and some pieces are not session-aware. Gaps are handled only by stop_gap and target_gap at the open, and only if a bar exists. The session counter appends a calendar date only when a bar is handled, so missing data days do not count. There is no gap-size guard and no corporate-action handling. build_clock excludes the last bar of each frame. EngineBPolicy defaults are 'prototype policy, not sealed calibration'. The cost model leg_cost is product-agnostic: the same intraday-style formula applies to a CNC carry. Orchestrator._leg_cost is bound to it directly. strict_session_boundary defaults True and closes at the session close once len(sessions) >= max_sessions. With it False, the max-sessions exit would run at the next session's open, after an extra overnight gap.
findings.impact: B P&L, carry cost and holding time are approximations. Do not use B results as calibration evidence.
findings.action: Add product-aware costs, a gap and halt policy, and calendar-aware session counting before treating B results as evidence.

findings.claim: Native plant latch and HRSG vs external hooks. The orchestrator drives only part of the native plant: begin_bar, grid_relay evaluation, open/close_grid_intertie, bays[].register_outcome, bay governors, and protection snapshots. It never calls CentralPlantMasterDCS.evaluate_entry, the only caller of apply_hrsg_balance. Nothing in the repo calls record_hrsg_return_snapshot or hrsg.superheat_headroom_factor. So during orchestrated replay HRSG capital routing, correlation damping (the correlation window stays empty, so penalties are 1.0) and superheat headroom are not on the execution path. Admission caps come from PlantControlChain and BayTurbineClosedLoopGovernor.cap_dispatch_entry (a proportional cap on gross notional, with no integral term). MiCOM trips are partly evaluated by an orchestrator-side duplicate (_micom_step) using relay.evaluate_grid_intertie. Native 'tripped_offline' for a bay also arises from register_outcome after two stops. External per-symbol symbol_tripped and bay loss cooldown (BAY_LOSS_COOLDOWN_BARS=15) run in parallel. The ECS _previous_demand starts at 0 (HOLD) and ramps up.
findings.impact: HRSG hardware is native-plant code that the replay engine does not touch. Statements that HRSG recovery, derating or superheat shape trading outcomes are unsupported by the call graph.
findings.action: Either wire evaluate_entry/HRSG into PAPER_APPLY with a test of the path, or document HRSG as unconnected. Treat protection state as duplicated in two places (orchestrator-side and native).

findings.claim: The note's HRSG 'profit recovery' description does not match the actual law. hrsg.py recovers capital, not profit. When a GTG bay is tripped_offline or has cooldown_bars_remaining>0 (a cooldown from a single loss counts), its base allocation is set to 0. recovery_fraction (default 0.60) of it is routed to healthy STG bays pro rata to their base allocations (equal split if the base total is 0). The remainder goes to reserve. An unavailable STG's capital goes to reserve and is not harvested. Pairwise return correlation above rho_crit (0.65) derates the allocation of bays toward min_penalty_factor 0.70, with the derate going to reserve. superheat_headroom_factor is keyed on recent expectancy in R: >=0.60 gives 1+max_superheat_boost (0.15), >=0.45 gives half of it, otherwise 1.0. It has no caller. The values are 'frozen design constants pending replay/calibration evidence'. Routed shares are added without re-applying the dispatcher's max_ceiling (0.35), so a bay could exceed the ceiling; this is a qualified risk read from the code, not verified numerically.
findings.impact: A note describing 'profit recovery' mis-states the control. It is capital re-routing plus correlation damping, triggered by bay unavailability, not by profit.
findings.action: Correct the note. State recovery_fraction as a fraction of curtailed GTG capital; flag the ceiling gap.

findings.claim: The standalone fleet PID is alternate/fleet_loading_controller.py (FleetLoadingController, FleetLoadingPolicy, new_risk_headroom_pu). Its own docstring says 'nothing imports this module yet', and a repo-wide grep finds no importer. The orchestrator, plant_control, the plant and the script do not reference it. Its policy default is enabled=False, so even if imported it would pass capacity through unchanged. The existing fleet loading path is different: the ECS demand setpoint, with bounded restore rate and one-way derates, plus the paper admission cap in cap_dispatch_entry. The module is self-consistent as a unit (conditional integration anti-windup, trip clears derivative memory, strict state restore), but no dt, reference or capacity source exists in the engine to feed it.
findings.impact: No engine behaviour depends on the fleet PID. Claims of fleet-PID loading control are not supported by the current import graph.
findings.action: Treat as a prototype. If wired, derive dt from replay timestamps, expose a reference and capacity source, and journal its export_state.

findings.claim: V3 identity. The three-loop controller actually instantiated is revision2_external.closed_loop_control.ClosedLoopSupervisor (imported at orchestrator.py:46 and constructed at 324), which implements its own observe_trade_path, observe_portfolio_risk and CausalOutcomeLedger. Neither orchestrator.py nor closed_loop_control.py references closed_loop_v3, and no other module in the snapshot imports it. ClosedLoopV3Tester, TradePathLoop and PortfolioRiskLoop in closed_loop_v3.py (which imports closed_loop_v2.EntryQualityLoop) are a separate research and test harness. The two have different constants and logic, so V3 test results do not transfer to the engine's loops.
findings.impact: V3 tests cover a controller the engine does not run.
findings.action: Test ClosedLoopSupervisor directly. Mark closed_loop_v3 as research only or delete it.

findings.claim: Authority modes. SHADOW (default plant_control_mode): the plant chain is computed and recorded, with no admission change. PAPER_APPLY: requires a real CentralPlantMasterDCS and a grid provider. It adds the _paper_plant_entry_limit cap (twice, at 1917-1925 and 1997-1999, fail-closed to quantity 0), the native begin_bar clock, and MiCOM relay evaluation and forced exits. governor_authority='advisory' (default) only records decisions. 'full' requires closed_loop_mode='active_paper' and a grid provider. The governor then gates entries and discretionary exits: the exit PID, HMM regime and path-loop actuations are demoted to ADVISORY_EXIT_NOT_ACTUATED, while hard stop, drawdown halt, MiCOM and force-close still outrank it. One narrow gap: a symbol failing upstream admission is skipped entirely, including exits, unless CC is on and a trade is open. Upstream admission is a static allow/deny and config check, so this is unlikely to trigger mid-run.
findings.impact: Behaviour differs materially per mode; evidence must name its mode.
findings.action: Keep a mode matrix in the audit report.

verdict: This is a source-reading verdict only; I executed nothing. The sealed candidate path (PAPER_APPLY, active_paper, governor advisory or full, in-memory plant, paper broker) is the default execution path. Its next-bar stop and exit ordering looks causally sound (F12), and plant/MiCOM/governor authority boundaries are explicit (F18). The optional layers are materially incomplete or unproven. The combined-cycle runtime, Engine B, durable restore, close-feedback recovery and conversion handling have no instantiation call site and no tests in this snapshot. Statically traced defects exist: product handling in the paper broker (F02, F03), non-atomic post-fill sequencing (F04), mutually exclusive and incomplete restart models (F05), silent failed exits (F08), and in-process-only close-feedback receipts (F07). The engine cannot run against the Kite adapter (F09). BrokerReconciliationService and the fleet PID are unwired (F10, F16). HRSG is not on the replay execution path (F14), and the note's 'profit recovery' wording misdescribes a capital-routing and correlation-damping law (F15). The instantiated closed-loop controller is ClosedLoopSupervisor, not closed_loop_v3 (F17). No assertion of completeness or correctness is made. Suggested harness checks, for the supervising agent to run: (1) a CC runtime test with one fill and one bar (F02); (2) conversion followed by re-entry in the same symbol (F03); (3) fault injection at 2036-2109 (F04); (4) a kill-and-restart test with an open position (F05); (5) a rejected exit order (F08); (6) a fake broker port with delayed, partial and unknown outcomes (F09, F11); (7) a call-graph test that asserts what the sealed script actually reaches.
